summary.intent: Get all open Dependabot PRs in the monokl repo passing CI, and decide what to do with PR #30 (ship release binaries and notify the Homebrew tap) now that the tap builds from source.
summary.outcome: PR #36 (removing the stray rust-toolchain.toml that broke Lint) was merged. The tiktoken-rs 0.12.1 API break in PR #34 was fixed in budget.rs, with the full suite of 713 tests passing, and committed and pushed to the Dependabot branch. Trimming notify-tap from #30 was requested but not yet done in this transcript.

repo: A stray rust-toolchain.toml on main caused Lint failures on PR #35 and the Dependabot PRs; removing it in #36 fixed Lint.
Dependabot PRs #32-#34 have CI runs predating #36's merge, so they need `@dependabot rebase` to pick up the fix.
PR #32 (install-action) and #33 (oxc group) otherwise pass Test, MSRV, Coverage, Audit and Changesets; only Lint (stale) and Entire Gates fail.

Entire Gates fails on every Dependabot PR but shows pending on the team's own PRs. The cause is likely Human Review, Up to Date or Agent Review settings in Entire (Settings → Gates), which is not code and cannot be read from the CLI.
The Homebrew tap's formulae build from source (depends_on rust) and publish their own bottles, so they do not use monokl's release binaries.

The tap's `autobump.yml` runs `brew bump --open-pr` daily using livecheck on `^monokl@…$` tags, so monokl needs no tap-specific workflow or secrets. This automation exists only on the tap's unmerged branches/PRs (#13-#15); tap main still has the older dispatch workflow.

PR #30's notify-tap job and monokl's access to TAP_APP_CLIENT_ID and TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY are unnecessary; what remains valuable in #30 is the four attested prebuilt archives for direct downloads or a proto plugin.
The pinned toolchain for the repo is Rust 1.98.1, and the code compiles and lints clean on it with the bumped dependencies.

code.finding: tiktoken-rs 0.12.1 makes `o200k_base_singleton()` return `&'static CoreBPE` without a mutex, so the `.lock()` call at this line no longer compiles. Dropping it fixed the build; switching to `encode_ordinary` was also planned, and token-count tests were unchanged.

workflow: Cargo cannot access its registry cache under ~/.cargo from inside the sandbox, so cargo commands had to be re-run outside it.
Committing onto a Dependabot branch stops Dependabot from rebasing it afterwards, so merge such PRs promptly or open your own bump PR.
Before answering about PR state, re-check live state with gh, since PRs merged and checks changed mid-session.
Running the known-strings token-count tests is a good way to confirm a tokenizer bump does not change behavior.

friction: Cargo registry cache access was blocked by the sandbox, forcing a retry outside it.
Entire Gates output lives on entire.com and could not be read from the CLI, so its failure cause on the Dependabot PRs is undiagnosed.
The user's reference to 'the PR' was initially ambiguous (#30 vs #36) and needed clarification.
The agent cannot issue `@dependabot rebase` comments on the user's behalf, leaving that to the user.
open_items: Trim the notify-tap job out of PR #30 (requested, not yet done); also decide whether to close #30 entirely or keep it for binaries only, and reword README install lines if closed.
Remove monokl from the org variable and secret's selected repos for TAP_APP_CLIENT_ID and TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY.
Comment `@dependabot rebase` on #32, #33 and #34 (if #34 isn't merged first) and on #35 to pick up the Lint fix from #36.
Diagnose the Entire Gates failure on Dependabot PRs (including #33) and decide whether to relax Human Review for the Dependabot actor.
Confirm that the `encode_ordinary` switch and 0.12.0's error-aware encoding changes were handled in budget.rs.
The tap's automation depends on unmerged tap PRs #13-#15, so the 'tap follows releases itself' claim holds only once they merge.
